Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  February 2, 2023

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on February
2, 2022, via Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:27 p.m.
followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Cynthia
  McLemore - District 3, Commissioner Christopher Beck- District 4,
  Commissioner Henry Brown -Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso - District 2

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor
  Geoffrey Okamoto  Transportation Supervisor
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner
McLemore that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on
August 4, 2022, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, McLemore, Beck and Brown
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Brown that
the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on November 3, 2022,
be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, Beck, Brown and McLemore
Noes: None

STAFF REPORTS.

Agreement for Administrative Services Cooperative, Inc. dba Yellow Cab, for Subsidized
Taxi Service for the Elderly and Disabled. Staff report dated February 2, 2023, was
presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission recommend the Mayor
and Council members take the following actions: 1) Approve the attached two-year
Agreement (with the option to extend an additional year), for the combined amount of
$150,000 per contract year, with administrative Services Cooperative, Inc. dba Yellow Cab
to provide subsidized taxicab services for elderly and disabled persons through February

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

27, 2025. (Grant Funds); and 2) Authorize payment of outstanding invoices for taxi services
provided from March 17, 2022, through February 28, 2023, in an amount not to exceed
$25,000.

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Fragoso that
the Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, Beck, McLemore, and Brown
Noes: None

Vincent Park Restroom Project Phase 2, CB-22-11. Staff report dated February 2, 2023,
was presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission recommend the
Mayor and Council members take the following actions: 1) Award the Vincent Park
Restroom Project Phase 2 (CB-22-11) to GA Builders, LLC, dba GA Construction; 2) Approve
an agreement in an amount not to exceed, $489,000; and 3) Authorize an additional City
controlled and directed ten percent (10%) contingency in the not-to-exceed amount of
$48,900 for a total cost of $537,900 per Bid No. CB-22-11. (General Fund)

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Brown that the
Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, Beck, Brown, and McLemore
Noes: None

Darby Park Restroom Project Phase 1, CB-22-03. Staff report dated February 2, 2023, was
presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission recommend the Mayor
and Council members take the following actions: 1) Adopt a Resolution voiding and/or
terminating Agreement No. 22-307 which was approved by the Council on September 13,
2022, to allow for correction of the amount noted for liquidated damages; and 2) Approve
new agreement with Doja, Inc. for the Darby Park Restroom Project in the amount of
$630,000 including the corrected liquidated damages amount; 3) Approve a City controlled
contingency in a not to exceed of $63,000 for a total project cost of $693,000. (General
Fund)

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner McLemore that the
Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Fragoso, McLemore, and Denmon
Noes: None

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. The Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez,
reported that the Parks Division has removed homeless encampments from Rogers,
Vincent and Darby Parks reservoirs. The Division acquired and will now maintain the center
medians on Centinela Avenue from La Tijera to Warren Lane. Graffiti Abatement continues
to remove Graffiti throughout the City in all Districts.

REPORTS - RECREATION. The Recreation Superintendent, Teresa Estrada, reported the
following: 1) City of Inglewood’s MLK Event: Due to torrential rains the City of Inglewood’s
Dr. Martin Luther King Day celebration was rescheduled to February 18, 2022 to coincide
with Black History Month. The event will take place along Market Street from 11 a.m. until
5 p.m. There will be two live stages, an assortment of great vendors, food booths and
trucks. One of our special guests will be Wendy Raquel Robinson from the hit television
show “The Game”. 2) Inglewood Youth Basketball League: The City of Inglewood in
partnership with the Los Angeles Clippers are proud to present a youth basketball league
to benefit the young people of Inglewood, ages 4-14. The League goals include
fundamental development, skill progression, team concepts and having fun. In 2023, the
league has more than doubled in size with 330 participants filling out 24 teams over six
divisions. Most importantly, we finally reached a goal of fielding a standalone all girls
league in the Tiny Might Division with girls ages 8-11. Season begins February 9, 2023 and
teams will compete over the course of the 9 weeks. The season will conclude by
celebrating all 24 teams in the final week with banquets consisting of food, fun, and awards
for all participants. For more information, visit our sports website at
www.cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com.

 REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. The Transportation Supervisor, Geoffrey Okamoto
reported the following: 1) Transportation Division continues to provide trips to critical
appointments as well as leisure trips to locations in and around Inglewood and Hawthorne.
Drivers as well as passengers continue to wear facemasks during transport. 2) Senior
Center Operations are steadily progressing forward with 34 classes/activities for seniors to
participate in; they include Line Dancing, Zumba, Gold, Knitting & Crochet, Ping Pong and
Bridge. A new class is coming, it will consist of seniors learning to navigate social media
platforms such a You Tube, Instagram, and Twitter. 3) Nutrition: Serving approximately
300 seniors per week and continue to provide fresh produce weekly, in collaboration with
the Social Justice Learning Institute. Home delivered meals continue to be provided to
those seniors who are homebound and congregate lunches at our Senior Center. In
December 2022, we had a tremendously successful festive party with 150 seniors enjoying
a special lunch and entertainment from our very own senior citizens choir the lunchroom
is set up to accommodate safe distancing and we look forward to continuing to provide
fresh prepared meals on a daily basis to our seniors. 4) (CACFP) the Child and Adult Car
Food Program serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at three sites

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

(Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park). The CACFP is on hold while we contract
a food vendor. The program’s hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from
2:30 p.m.-3:30 p.m. and snacks from 4:30 p.m. – 5:30 p.m., serving an average of 70 meals
per day at all three (3) sites.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. The Senior Management Assistant, Stephanie Maldonado reported
on Capital Improvement updates: 1) Construction of the new restroom at Edward Vincent
Park has been completed and once the installation of the electrical meter by Edison is
done, the restrooms will be open. 2) We will be going to Council for the Edward Vincent
Jr. Park restroom project-restroom number two (2) in February. The Darby Park restroom
was delayed due a discrepancy in the agreement. The new agreement will be presented to
the City Council on February 28, 2023. 3) The pump track is officially under construction as
of February 1, 2023. It is expected to take 8 to 10 weeks weather permitting. 4) Rain in
January had us to revisit the construction schedule for the Dodgers Dream field
renovations; the project is still on track to be completed by mid-May. 5) Other projects at
Edward Vincent Jr. Park include a restriping of the parking lots by champions field. We are
working with Public Works to have that work done. Plans to renovate the picnic arbors are
still active, hoping the project will go forward in the next 45-60 days.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown commended staff. Commissioner
McLemore thanked staff for reports. Commissioner asked if the cameras at Vincent Park
have been installed.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:51 p.m.
